Adaptive Facade

A Climate-Responsive Kinetic Building Envelope

In this project

Project briefResearch methodsProcess & experimentsOutcomes

Project brief

Adaptive Facade explores the potential of kinetic building envelopes to mediate environmental conditions through responsive geometry and integrated energy systems. Designed for Suzhou's subtropical monsoon climate, the project proposes a modular facade system incorporating movable thin-film photovoltaic panels. By adjusting their configurations in response to solar conditions, the facade explores how dynamic shading, daylight regulation, and solar energy harvesting can be integrated into a single architectural system. Through investigations into geometric configurations, kinetic mechanisms, energy conversion, and shading performance, the project examines how building envelopes can move beyond passive enclosure to actively mediate the relationship between architecture and its environment.

Research methods

Climate Analysis, Parametric Kinetic Design, Shading Performance Analysis, Physical Prototyping
